summary: Iteration 9: verified role normalization + name preservation. Backend: 4/4 pytest cases pass (canonical roles for all 141 users, known users in Proper Case, import preview normalizes role, import commit persists canonical role + preserves Proper Case names with accents). Frontend: all badges on /usuarios are colored (no gray) — Admin=dark navy/yellow, Supervisor=fuchsia (rgb(192,38,211)), Empleado=emerald (rgb(5,150,105)). Screenshot confirms visual correctness across 21+ rows including cmarin (Carlos Marín) and jdolande (José Dolande García) which retain Proper Case.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1565 lines — consider splitting into routers (users, attendance, sites, schedules, imports) for maintainability.
Startup backfill loops over every user with role and issues per-doc updates; acceptable for 141 users but should use bulk_write for larger datasets.
normalize_role() default-falls-back to 'employee' for unknown strings — safe, but consider logging when a fallback happens during import so users see it in the errors tab.
seed_data_creation: Import test creates TEST_qa_* users then deletes them at end of test_import_commit_role_and_name.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Role normalization + startup backfill + frontend ROLE_ALIASES all working. 141 users all have canonical role in DB. Badge rendering on /usuarios visually confirmed colored for all rows.
rca of the issue: Original bug: DB had mixed 'Empleado'/'employee' etc.; frontend ROLE_LABEL only keyed lowercase English. Fix: (a) server normalize_role() applied on import preview + commit, (b) startup migration unifies existing DB values, (c) frontend normalizeRole() folds all aliases before badge lookup. All three layers verified.
